title: Platform systems & services — Ops guide, dashboards, runbooks, roadmap (Q2 2026)
author: Sophie Nguyen
content:
## Summary

This document consolidates the platform systems & services operational guidance: service inventory and owners, dashboards and alerting standards, primary runbooks for high-impact incidents, how-to procedures for common platform tasks, a compact Q2 roadmap, and high-level retrospective notes from recent incidents. It is intended as the canonical team wiki for on-call engineers, SREs, and platform engineers.

Owner: eng-platform team. Primary contact: Sophie Nguyen (sophie@redwood.example).

## Goals
- Keep core platform SLOs stable: 99.9% availability for hosted API, p95 generation latency targets per model class.
- Reduce mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for critical incidents to under 10 minutes.
- Standardize dashboards and alert thresholds to reduce paging noise by 30%.
- Provide clear runbooks and escalation paths for top 5 incident classes.

## Service inventory (high level)
- routing-proxy (owner: platform-networking) — routes user requests to region/model pools; SLO: 99.95% uptime
- inference-gateway (owner: serving-runtime) — request shaping, auth, prefix-cache; SLO: 99.9% uptime, p95 latency 120ms for small-models
- gpu-autoscaler (owner: infra-autoscale) — cluster scaling for Dedicated pools; SLO: scale-to-capacity within 180s (target)
- kv-cache (owner: serving-runtime) — prefix/KV cache service; SLO: cache hit-rate >= 65% for production routes
- metrics-collector (owner: eng-observability) — collects Prometheus metrics & traces

## Ownership and escalation
- Primary on-call: eng-platform rotation (see team wiki for schedule)
- Escalation path:
  1) Primary on-call (eng-platform) — initial mitigation, runbook steps
  2) Secondary on-call (serving-runtime) — escalate if impact > 10% customer requests or not mitigated within 10 min
  3) Pager duty to Eng SRE lead and Engineering manager for severity >= sev2 incidents

## Dashboards and alerting standards
Guidelines: dashboards should answer the question: is the service healthy, is customer traffic impacted, what is the likely root cause? Alerts should be actionable, with runbook links and a single mitigation first step. Avoid duplicate alerts for the same root cause.

Recommended dashboards (names and primary charts):
- Platform Overview
  - cluster availability by region
  - 1m error-rate and 5m error-rate for all API routes
  - overall token throughput and cost estimate
- Inference Gateway: Latency & Errors
  - p50/p95/p99 request latency over time
  - 5xx error rate by backend pool
  - active KV cache hit rate
- GPU Fleet Health
  - GPU utilization per rack
  - OOM counts and driver restarts
  - node-level temperature and thermal throttling events

Alert threshold table (examples):
| Alert name | Trigger | Severity | First action (runbook) | Owner |
|------------|---------|----------|------------------------|-------|
| inference-latency-p95-high | p95 latency > 2x target for 5m | sev2 | validate recent deploys, throttle non-critical routes | serving-runtime |
| inference-5xx-spike | error rate > 1% for 2 min and delta > 3x baseline | sev2 | identify failing pool, failover to compatible model variant | serving-runtime |
| gpu-oom-rate-high | OOM events > 3 in 10m per node group | sev1 | cordon node, drain pods, notify infra-autoscale | infra-autoscale |
| kv-cache-hit-low | cache hit-rate < 40% for 10m | sev3 | review cache invalidations and recent rollout | serving-runtime |

Alerting best-practices:
- Every alert must include a link to the specific runbook and a one-line mitigation.
- Use composite alerts to reduce duplicate pages (example: combine latency + 5xx increase).
- Notify Slack channel #platform-ops for sev3+, @on-call for sev2/1.

## Key runbooks (quick reference)
1) High p95 latency on inference-gateway
   - 1) Triage: open Platform Overview dashboard, confirm p95 across regions.
   - 2) Check recent deploys: rwdctl deploy list --since 1h
   - 3) If error rate elevated on specific backend pool: failover traffic to secondary pool via routing-proxy console (link: /routing-proxy/runbooks/failover).
   - 4) If KV cache miss spike: increase cache TTL temporarily and flush suspect prefixes: rwdctl cache flush --prefix problematic-prefix
   - 5) If GPU saturation: trigger emergency scale (see GPU OOM runbook)
   - 6) Post-mortem ticket and retrospective within 72 hours.

2) GPU OOM / driver restarts (sev1)
   - 1) Immediate: mark node as unschedulable: kubectl cordon <node>
   - 2) Drain pods with graceful timeout 30s: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
   - 3) Check dmesg and driver logs; collect via rwdctl node collect-logs <node> --since 1h
   - 4) If multiple nodes affected: scale down traffic to affected region and notify infra-autoscale on-call.
   - 5) Preserve node for debugging if OOM pattern unclear, attach to case.

3) Autoscaler stuck (GPU fleet does not add nodes)
   - 1) Confirm API calls to cloud provider: check autoscaler logs and last successful API response.
   - 2) Validate IAM credentials for autoscaler service account.
   - 3) As temporary mitigation: move lower-priority workloads to other pools or enable burst capacity pool.

## How-to procedures
- Adding a new dashboard
  1) Create a new dashboard under folder eng-platform/Platform Dashboards with a short description and owner.
  2) Include at least one traffic, one latency, and one error chart.
  3) Add README widget with runbook link and on-call contact.
  4) Peer review: request review from eng-observability and serving-runtime.

- Updating alert thresholds
  1) Open the alert in the alert manager UI and propose new threshold with justification (attach traffic distribution).
  2) Run a dry-run using the simulate rule tool: rwdctl alerts simulate --rule <rule-id> --historical 7d
  3) Once agreed, schedule change during a maintenance window if the change affects sev1/2 alerts.

- Onboarding a new service to platform monitoring
  1) Create service owner entry in Service Inventory spreadsheet and assign primary on-call.
  2) Add Prometheus metrics with standard labels (service, env, region, pool).
  3) Create dashboard with standard panels and a set of initial alerts.
  4) Run crash-fire drill with the service owner to validate runbooks.

## Roadmap (Q3 2026 highlights)
- Centralized incident timeline view in Console (owner: eng-platform) — deliverable: Sept 2026
- Automatic alert noise reduction using anomaly detection on token throughput (pilot) — deliverable: Aug 2026
- Improved autoscaler diagnostics with cloud provider call traces — deliverable: July 2026
- Runbook runner: a light orchestration layer to execute first-step mitigations automatically for < 5m remediations — research/POC ongoing

## Retrospective notes (last 3 months)
- Incident: region-eu latency spike (May 2026)
  - Root cause: misconfiguration in route weights after a canary deploy; mitigation: rollback to previous route config.
  - Actions: add a pre-deploy route weight validation check, improved Canary monitor to detect sudden p95 jumps within 10 minutes.
- Incident: GPU OOM burst (April 2026)
  - Root cause: new model variant had regression in memory growth for long contexts.
  - Actions: add memory regression checks to model onboarding; require memory cap tests in CI for serving.

## Post-incident action items (owner & ETA)
- Add route-weight pre-deploy validator (owner: platform-networking, ETA: 2026-08-01)
- Model memory cap test in CI (owner: applied-ml, ETA: 2026-07-25)
- Alert deduplication pilot (owner: eng-observability, ETA: 2026-09-15)

## Appendix: useful CLI snippets
- Simulate alerts on historical data:
``
rwdctl alerts simulate --rule inference-latency-p95-high --historical 14d
```
- Flush KV cache for prefix (use with caution):
``
rwdctl cache flush --prefix user:session:abc123
```
- Emergency failover to backup pool:
``
rwdctl routing failover --from-pool pool-a --to-pool pool-a-secondary --reason "auto-mitigation"
```

For questions or to propose edits, open a PR against this page and add the appropriate reviewers.
